items.title: Christchurch terrorist in fiery exchanges in NZ Court of Appeal
items.description: The convicted Christchurch terrorist and murderer is giving testimony in the New Zealand Court of Appeal as he seeks to vacate his guilty pleas over his 2019 attack on two mosques.

items.title: Live: Isaac Herzog lays wreath at Bondi to commemorate victims of antisemitic attack
items.description: Israeli President Isaac Herzog has arrived in Sydney for a four-day visit following the Bondi Beach terror attack. Follow live.

items.title: Herzog says 'we shall overcome this evil together' during Bondi visit
items.description: Isaac Herzog was invited by the governor-general and prime minister to join the Jewish community grieving the loss of life in the December 14 massacre of mostly Jewish Australians at a Hanukkah event.

items.title: Independent inquiry launched into NACC chief's handling of defence ties
items.description: The body responsible for holding the federal integrity watchdog to account will formally investigate it for agency maladministration and its chief, Paul Brereton, for officer misconduct.

items.title: What the Epstein files tell us about Ghislaine Maxwell
items.description: This week, Ghislaine Maxwell could be a very unwelcome distraction for Donald Trump as she appears before one of America's top political institutions.

items.title: Live: Seattle Seahawks win Super Bowl LX after dominant performance
items.description: The Seattle Seahawks are champions of the NFL, defeating the New England Patriots 29-13 in Super Bowl LX. Follow live.

items.title: Live: Ley ally warns colleagues they'll be criticised for 'political assassination'
items.description: Shadow Attorney-General Andrew Wallace has warned Liberal colleagues that any move to roll Ley will be seen as "political assassination". Follow live.

items.title: Liberals despair at prospect of 'non-existence' and weigh leadership change
items.description: Sussan Ley could face a challenge to her leadership from Angus Taylor this week after a disastrous opinion poll showed the Coalition parties falling further behind One Nation.

items.title: Hong Kong media mogul Jimmy Lai sentenced to 20 years' jail in landmark case
items.description: Jimmy Lai, one of Hong Kong's most outspoken critics of China, has learned his fate after being sentenced this morning.

items.title: Two dead in head-on crash after utility driven on wrong side of freeway
items.description: A 56-year-old-woman and a 24-year-old man are dead after a head-on collision involving a utility that was being driven on the wrong side of the Mitchell Freeway in Perth's north.

items.title: 'My heart broke for her': Rivals heap praise on 'idol' Vonn after crash
items.description: Lindsey Vonn's 2026 Winter Olympic Games ended in disaster, but her teammates and rivals have heaped praise on the three-time Olympic medallist.

items.title: Young people could get massive pay boost in 'totemic' wage case
items.description: "I'm paying adult fuel with still a child's wage," says Ben Walker, one of the almost half a million young people who could see a huge boost to their wage.

items.title: HESTA chief executive resigns after superannuation outage
items.description: HESTA's boss is calling it quits after 11 years in the role. Her exit follows an outage that left members unable to access their accounts.

items.title: Jon Kudelka, cartoonist and 'national treasure', dies aged 53
items.description: Award-winning Tasmanian cartoonist Jon Kudelka has died after being diagnosed with brain cancer in 2024.

items.title: Rain brings relief and road closures after record heatwave in SA
items.description: High rainfall in north-eastern South Australia brings some relief for pastoralists after record-breaking heat, with a reprieve expected for metropolitan Adelaide this week.

items.title: Live: ASX rallies strongly after Wall Street rebound
items.description: The ASX has rebounded strongly after dropping 1.8 per cent last week. Follow the day's events and insights from our business reporters on the ABC News live markets blog.

items.title: Quiz: How well do you know this week in history?
items.description: Groundhog Day, an audacious art theft and a new chief mouser: how well do you remember these events?

items.title: One Nation capitalises on decades of Australian migration policy
items.description: Pauline Hanson might not have any substantive policies, but her rhetoric about reducing migration is clearly finding an audience.

items.title: Liberals and Nationals reunite without fixing their identity crises
items.description: The Coalition has reunited, but the new agreement does not address underlying party tensions nor the surging fragmentation of the right.

items.title: Prickly businessman tied to massive tobacco fine says there's a deeper story
items.description: He's been declared bankrupt repeatedly, and was a gambling addict. Now he's linked to a $1.5 million fine for illegal tobacco.

items.title: Psychedelic PTSD treatment for veterans to be funded under $740m plan
items.description: A $740 million program will expand support for veterans and include funding for social activities such as yoga and language classes, with new treatment including MDMA and psilocybin for the worst forms of PTSD also funded for the first time.

items.title: Tropical Cyclone Mitchell downgraded to category one system
items.description: Residents are sheltering as destructive winds and heavy rain lash the tourist towns in north-west WA.

items.title: Mother claims missed warning signs in NT hospital led to baby's disabilities
items.description: Mia Pilbrow is taking legal action against a Northern Territory hospital and calling for the territory to adopt tailored pre-term labour guidelines, after medical staff sent her home seven times during her pregnancy, repeatedly assuring her the baby was fine.

items.title: Iranian Nobel Peace Prize winner sentenced to further jail time
items.description: Women's rights activist Narges Mohammadi is sentenced to a further six years in jail.

items.title: Bail law amendments result in more First Nation remands, researchers find
items.description: A study has found increasing "punitive" bail law amendments are negatively affecting First Nations people.
